title: Minimax Estimation of Affected-Patient Effects of a Rarely Binding High-Dose Cap
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier incremental below floor field; paper_score_ceiling 5.9 < 7.4. The note proves two-sided finite-sample order bounds, but the rate follows from a direct window estimator and a standard tent/modulus argument in a known triangular-design class.
gap_reasons: The note proves two-sided finite-sample order bounds for estimation and honest connected-interval length, including the flat-response lower bound, but only in a one-dimensional experiment with an exactly known triangular assignment density and a fixed Lipschitz class.

The rate follows from a direct window estimator and a standard tent/modulus argument, while the related-work discussion does not establish that evaluating general optimal-recovery theory for this particular moving contrast constitutes a field-level methodological advance.
These scope and novelty limitations keep the package below the field floor despite the matched order statements.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved matched finite-sample absolute-risk and honest-interval length orders, the flat-response lower bound, and the moving-contrast modulus for a known triangular dose design. A post-halt repair widened the response class, corrected the prior-work positioning, and independently cleared all three math-panel findings; only exact sharp elbow constants remain open. The field-tier novelty claim failed because the delivered window/tent argument in this stylized known-design model did not establish a field-level methodological advance; an unknown-density extension would require a new proposal.
tldr: A high-dose cap changes treatment only in a tail of probability \(\delta^2\). In the one-time randomized specialization of generalized affected-subset treatment effects, arbitrary binary potential outcomes reduce observationally to Bernoulli regression with mean \(\mu\), and the affected-patient effect is a moving point response minus a weighted tail average. This contrast cancels constants and has range of order \(\delta\), unlike the retained-natural-course clamp mean. Uniformly for every \(n\geq1\) and \(0<\delta\leq1/4\), minimax absolute risk and \(90\%\)-honest connected-interval length are of order \(\min\{\delta,(n\delta)^{-1/3}\}\), with transition at \(n\delta^4\asymp1\). The upper bounds hold for the full arbitrary binary randomized class; a threshold-rank tent is used only as an embedded submodel for the lower bounds, including expected-length nonadaptation at the flat response.
gap: Susmann, Williams, Rudolph, and D\'iaz supply the generalized affected-subset identification bridge, and the retained-natural-course clamp paper supplies a frontier for a different functional. Neither gives a uniform moving-cap frontier for the normalized point-minus-tail contrast or an honest-length lower bound at a flat response.
fill: The paper derives the contrast-versus-clamp separation, its exact contracting range, an explicit centered known-design estimator, a bias-aware connected interval, a single legal tent for both lower regimes, and a weighted-\(L^2\) modulus that matches the finite-sample rate.
